verdict.rationale: Aider documents several built-in event-triggered behaviors. `--watch-files` acts when a saved file contains an `AI!` or `AI?` comment, `--auto-test` with `--test-cmd` runs your test suite after each AI edit, and edited files are auto-linted. These are fixed triggers with a configurable command, not a general rule engine where users define their own event→action rules. missing for 10: user-defined arbitrary event/condition rules (a hooks system), triggers beyond file-save comments and post-edit events, documentation of rule composition, independent hands-on corroboration of trigger reliability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can configure aider to run your test suite after each time the AI edits your code using the --test-cmd <test-command> and --auto-test switch.
AI! triggers aider to make changes to your code.
If you run aider with `--watch-files`, it will watch all files in your repo and look for any AI coding instructions you add using your favorite IDE or text editor.
By default, aider will lint any files which it edits.
